module.title: Sea ice: viscous-plastic dynamics and multi-category thermodynamics
entrypoints: verification/lab_sea (input, input.hb87, input.fd, input.salt_plume, input.natl_box, input.longstep)
verification/offline_exf_seaice (input, input.dyn_lsr, input.dyn_jfnk, input.dyn_paralens, input.dyn_mce, input.dyn_teardrop, input.dyn_ellnnfr, input.thermo, input.thsice)
module.expensive_path: The viscous-plastic momentum solve in seaice_dynsolver.F: the LSR line-successive-over-relaxation solver (seaice_lsr.F, hundreds of sweeps per step), the EVP sub-cycled explicit solver (seaice_evp.F), and the JFNK/Krylov Newton solvers (seaice_jfnk.F, seaice_krylov.F) each recompute the strain-rate, viscosity (seaice_calc_viscosities.F) and stress fields on every iteration; plus the multidimensional advection of area, thickness, snow and ITD categories (seaice_advdiff.F) and the per-category growth (seaice_growth.F). In coupled Arctic runs the ice dynamics is a large fraction of the time step.
module.rationale: pkg/seaice is a closed physics component with its own state (area, heff, hsnow, uice, vice, ITD categories), its own solvers and its own verification decks; it is the target of the Veris JAX port (Koutian Wu's PR #34) and can be exercised with the ocean frozen (offline_exf_seaice) or coupled (lab_sea). thsice is the alternative thermodynamics that pkg/seaice can delegate to, and salt_plume is a sea-ice-only source term, so both belong with it.
excluded: pkg/exf and pkg/cal (forcing and calendar) are shared infrastructure the checks depend on but the module does not own
Ocean dynamics under the ice (model/src, cg2d) belong to mitgcm-ocean-dynamics; lab_sea checks grade the ice fields
Adjoint decks (input_ad*, input_tap*) need TAF/Tapenade and are out of scope
hazards: One build per deck: each check compiles its own mitgcmuv (one to three minutes) from the candidate tree
lab_sea writes 32-bit output by default (writeBinaryPrec=32); checks set 64
Keep nPx=nPy=1: MPI ranks change the cg2d global-sum order at round-off level

approval.human_ref: looks rather nice, lets go? (2026-09-02, all six modules approved; package mitgcm-seaice first)
